sections.h2: Northport and its neighbor across the river
sections.html:
Northport sits in Tuscaloosa County on the north bank of the Black Warrior River, straight across from downtown Tuscaloosa. It incorporated in 1871 and belongs to the Tuscaloosa metro area. Many residents work in Tuscaloosa or elsewhere in the county, so a Northport house is shopped against the whole two-city market. Your listing competes for the same buyers as a house on the other side of the water.

The 2020 census counted 31,125 residents, which made Northport the 17th most populous city in Alabama. The city grew by 33.4 percent between 2010 and 2020. It had 13,382 housing units that year, with 6.8 percent vacant, and a rental vacancy rate of 7.8 percent.

Fast growth puts newer subdivisions next to older streets, so an older house has newer comparables close by. That gap in age and condition is usually what makes a repair-heavy sale hard to price. ZIP codes in the city are 35473, 35475 and 35476.

The University of Alabama is the largest employer in Tuscaloosa County, and Northport falls inside its commuting range. The county's median age was only 32.9 in 2020, and 41.1 percent of occupied homes there were renter-occupied. County rental vacancy was 11.6 percent. For the owner of a small Northport rental, that means regular tenant changes, repainting, cleaning and surprise repairs.

Home football Saturdays reshape the calendar. Bryant-Denny Stadium holds 100,077 people, and traffic around town changes on fall weekends. Schedule showings away from kickoff.

The Black Warrior Parkway is a 4.9 mile toll road linking Tuscaloosa and Northport, and cars pay $1.50 in cash. Interstate 20/59, US 43 and US 82 serve the county. Tuscaloosa National Airport and Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport are both in reach, and the Amtrak Crescent stops at the Tuscaloosa station.

A house with an easy route to the interstate or to US 43 sits close to many county workplaces, including the hospitals, school systems and manufacturers. Buyers who commute between the two cities will ask about the toll road, so mention it.

Northport belongs to the Tuscaloosa County School System, which serves county residents outside the Tuscaloosa city limits, and not to Tuscaloosa City Schools. Tuscaloosa County High School is in Northport. Buyers comparing both cities often ask about zoning, so confirm the school assignment for your address with the district before you advertise it.

Central Alabama is tornado country. A 1932 tornado wrecked parts of Northport, including a lumber mill. On April 27, 2011, an EF4 tornado about half a mile wide hit Tuscaloosa in the Super Outbreak, killing at least 44 people there and injuring more than 1,000. It is still the reference point for storm talk across the metro area.

Buyers and their insurers may ask about roof age, past storm damage and whether the house has a safe room or interior shelter. If the house has had hail or wind claims, have the paperwork ready. It makes the history easy to explain, and it shows buyers the repairs were done properly.

The Kentuck Festival of the Arts has drawn 10,000 to 20,000 visitors a year, and Kentuck Park is slated for development as a sports complex. Residents have raised concerns about noise, traffic and effects on nearby home values. If you live near that park or the planned water park, expect buyers to ask about both.

Every Alabama deed carries a recordation tax of 50 cents on each $500 of value, set by Code section 40-22-1. Before the deed can be recorded, the probate judge has to receive that tax, and a separate recording fee applies.

Each year the property tax bill is due October 1 and goes delinquent after December 31, so a fall closing may overlap the bill. Settle in the contract who pays it. Tuscaloosa County keeps parcel records and sends the bills. Request a payoff figure from the county before choosing a closing day, and tell the title company whether this year's bill is paid.

sections.h2: Selling with a loan or taxes owed
sections.html:
A mortgage or a tax bill will not block a sale. Before closing, the title company requests a lender payoff letter and the county's current tax figure. Both come out of the proceeds, and you receive whatever is left.

Liens, unpaid utilities and code fines surface in the title search and get cleared the same way. Not sure what is recorded against your lot? Request the search early and read it before picking a date.

For an inherited Northport house, the first job is proving who has authority to sign. Talk with the probate office or an attorney about that paperwork before you ask anyone for an offer. A closing cannot happen without it.

A little preparation saves time. Walk through the house and list every flaw, however ugly: roof leaks, tired air conditioning, water stains, a tenant who is behind on rent. A frank list produces an offer that holds up, since nothing surprises the buyer on a second visit.

Pull together the deed, the newest tax bill, your mortgage statement and any storm or insurance claim records. A rented house also needs the lease and rent history. When offers arrive, set each one against the likely net from a listing, after repairs, fees and carrying costs, and pick what fits your timeline.

Cash works when speed, condition or a tenant problem outweighs the higher price a repaired listing might reach. Around Northport you will see:

  • A campus-area rental that needs paint, flooring and a deep clean once the lease ends.
  • A family house left behind, with no heir who wants to keep up the yard and repairs.
  • A house with storm, roof or water damage that would fail a financed buyer's inspection.

The usual order goes like this. You describe the house and any tenant. We respond with an offer based on the condition. If you accept, a title company reviews ownership records and schedules a closing on a date that suits you. It settles the mortgage and unpaid taxes at closing, and you keep the remainder.

Bring a photo ID, the deed or estate paperwork, any mortgage statement and, for a rented house, a copy of the lease and the move-out date. Cleaning out the house and fixing it up are not required.

We buy Northport houses as they are, and you decide whether to accept an offer. Compare it with what a listing could net after repairs, agent fees and the months a vacant house may sit.

faqs.a: Tuscaloosa County, in west central Alabama, on the north bank of the Black Warrior River.
No. Northport is its own city, incorporated in 1871. It shares a boundary and a metro area with Tuscaloosa.

faqs.q: How much is the Alabama deed tax?
faqs.a: The state charges 50 cents per $500 of value conveyed under Alabama Code section 40-22-1. The probate office collects it before recording the deed.

faqs.q: When do Northport property taxes come due?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental with tenants in Northport?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase an occupied house or one that needs work. Share the lease terms and the condition so the offer reflects them.
